system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: In June 2019, Sunee defaulted on one instalment. The contract provided that on any default the creditor could charge default interest on the entire outstanding balance. At that time, was such a clause void under a specific provision of the Civil and Commercial Code? Answer briefly.
raw_response:
Yes, such a clause was void under **Section 654 of the Civil and Commercial Code**.

Section 654 specifically provides that any stipulation allowing a creditor to charge default interest on the **entire outstanding balance** when only one instalment is in default is **void**. 

The provision requires that default interest may only be charged on the **instalment(s) actually in default**, not on the full remaining debt. This protects debtors from disproportionate penalty clauses in instalment contracts.

Since Sunee defaulted on only one instalment in June 2019, the contractual clause purporting to allow default interest on the entire outstanding balance would have been unenforceable under Section 654.
